title: Closest Drop-off Points
statement: A delivery drone starts at (0, 0). `points[i] = [x, y]` is a drop-off point. Return the `k` points closest to the start (straight-line distance), ordered from closest to farthest; break ties by smaller x, then smaller y.
constraints: Compare x*x + y*y; no square root needed

answerKey.pattern: Max-heap of size k keyed by distance (or a min-heap over all points)
keyPoints: Compare squared distances to avoid square roots
Keep a max-heap of the k closest so far; pop the farthest when it grows past k
Sort the k survivors by distance, then x, then y for the output order
answerKey.timeComplexity: O(n log k + k log k)
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Sort all points by (distance, x, y) and take the first k: O(n log n)

hints: Do you need the actual distance, or is something simpler enough to compare?
Keep only k candidates. Which one should leave when a closer point arrives?
A max-heap by distance holds the k closest; sort them at the end with the tie rules.
